sentences.ko: 작별 인사 한 번 받으려면 내가 뭘 해야 되는데?
sentences.text: What do I got to do to get a goodbye?

alts.text: Is there something I need to do in order to receive a goodbye?

sentences.note: **What do I got to do to** 는 문법대로라면 What do I have to do 지만, 실제 말에서는 이렇게 많이 씁니다. 인사도 없이 가려는 사람한테 서운한 마음을 장난스럽게 드러낼 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: I have job security for life, you know.

alts.text: Can't ever get fired, you know.
My position is secure for the rest of my life.

sentences.note: **job security** 는 회사에서 잘릴 걱정이 없는 것을 말합니다. **for life** 를 붙이면 '평생'이 되고, 끝에 붙인 **you know** 는 상대도 아는 사실을 가볍게 짚을 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그쪽에서 부른 값에서 한 푼도 못 깎아 준대.
sentences.text: They said they wouldn't go a penny under the asking price.

alts.text: Apparently they won't budge on the price.
The sellers stated that they would not accept anything below the asking price.

sentences.note: **asking price** 는 파는 사람이 처음 부른 값이고, **a penny under** 는 '한 푼이라도 아래로'라는 뜻입니다. 집이나 중고차 값을 흥정하다 안 됐을 때 그대로 쓸 수 있는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 이건 꼭 말해야겠는데, 너희 엄마 책 진짜 좋아해.
sentences.text: I GOT TO TELL YOU, I LOVE YOUR MOM'S BOOKS.

alts.text: Gotta say, big fan of your mom's books.
I must say, I truly enjoy your mother's books.

sentences.note: **I GOT TO TELL YOU** 는 '이건 꼭 말하고 싶은데' 하고 칭찬이나 솔직한 말을 꺼내기 전에 붙입니다. 처음 만난 자리에서 상대 가족 이야기를 칭찬할 때 자연스럽습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 차려입고 원래 내가 아닌 사람인 척하는 거.
sentences.text: Dressing up and pretending to be someone you're not.

alts.text: Getting all dressed up and acting like somebody else.
Wearing a costume and pretending to be a different person.

sentences.note: **pretending to be someone you're not** 는 '나답지 않게 다른 사람인 척하는 것'으로, 억지로 꾸미는 자리를 말할 때 자주 씁니다. **Dressing up** 은 차려입는 것과 분장하는 것을 둘 다 가리킵니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 8 | Friends

sentences.text: This was supposed to be a temp job.

alts.text: Only meant to be a temp gig.
I had intended this to be only a temporary position.

sentences.note: **was supposed to be**는 '원래 ~이기로 했던 건데 (지금은 아니다)'라는 아쉬움을 담아요. 생각보다 오래 붙잡혀 있는 일이나 상황을 두고 푸념할 때 써요. **temp job**은 임시직이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 응, 그 사람이 카펫을 다 걷어내서 이제 소리가 다 들려.
sentences.text: Yeah, he took up the carpets and now you can hear everything.

alts.text: Yep, the carpet's gone, so every little sound comes through.
Yes, he removed the carpets, and now every sound can be heard.

sentences.note: **took up the carpets**의 take up은 바닥에 깔린 것을 '걷어내다'라는 뜻이에요. 층간소음이나 이웃 소음을 하소연할 때 **you can hear everything**을 그대로 쓰면 돼요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 정말 기뻤는데, 그 사람을 최대한 빨리 우리 집에서 내보내고 싶은 마음뿐이었어.
sentences.text: I was so happy and all I wanted was to get her out of my apartment as fast as possible.

alts.text: Honestly I was thrilled, but I just wanted her gone ASAP.
Although I was very happy, my only wish was for her to leave my apartment as quickly as possible.

sentences.note: **all I wanted was**는 '바라는 건 오직 ~뿐이었다'라는 말로, 다른 건 다 필요 없고 그것 하나만 바랐다고 강조할 때 써요. **as fast as possible**은 '최대한 빨리'예요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아, 그리고 미리 말해 두는데, 우리 아직 걔한테 입양된 거 말 안 했어.
sentences.text: Uh, by the way, you should know we haven't told him he's adopted yet.

alts.text: Oh, heads up — he doesn't know he's adopted.
Incidentally, I should mention that we have not yet told him that he is adopted.

sentences.note: **by the way**에 **you should know**를 붙이면 '참고로 알아 둬'라는 뜻이 돼요. 상대가 실수하지 않도록 미리 귀띔할 때 써요. 캐주얼 말투에서는 **heads up**이 같은 역할을 해요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends
